q: Physics, like any other branch of science, is based on systematic observations and precise ____.
e: Physics, like any other branch of science, is based on systematic observations and precise measurements. Measurements here means a comparison with an agreed standard that gives you a number. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: Most experiments in Physics require the observations made to be ____ rather than qualitative.
e: Most experiments in Physics require the observations made to be quantitative rather than qualitative. Quantitative here means observations written as numbers, not just hot or cold. Hot or cold is not enough; the lab needs a number.

Measurement essentially is a comparison process. Comparison here means matching an unknown amount against an agreed standard. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: A standard quantity of some kind, referred to as a ____, is first established.
e: A standard quantity of some kind, referred to as a unit, is first established. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.

q: ____ is something or a reference used as a measure for length, mass and time.
e: Standard is something or a reference used as a measure for length, mass and time. Standard here means the reference you compare length, mass, or time against.

q: Unit is a quantity or an amount used as a ____ of measurement.
e: Unit is a quantity or an amount used as a standard of measurement. Standard here means the reference you compare length, mass, or time against. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.
These things are known as 'physical quantities'. Physical quantities names these things.

q: A physical quantity is the quantity that can be measured, and consists of a numerical magnitude and a ____.
e: A physical quantity is the quantity that can be measured, and consists of a numerical magnitude and a unit. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.
It can be expressed as $Q=Nu$. The physics in this sentence is built around $Q=Nu$.

q: where Q is the physical quantity, N is a ____ and u is the unit.
e: Where Q is the physical quantity, N is a dimensionless number and u is the unit. The physics in this sentence is built around dimensionless number.

q: Physical quantities can be classified as the basic type and the ____ type.
e: Physical quantities can be classified as the basic type and the derived type. The physics in this sentence is built around derived.

q: A derived unit is a unit of measurement formed by ____ the basic (or base) units of a system.
e: A derived unit is a unit of measurement formed by combining the basic (or base) units of a system. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: A physical quantity is the quantity that can be measured, and consists of a ____ and a unit.
e: A physical quantity is the quantity that can be measured, and consists of a numerical magnitude and a unit. The physics in this sentence is built around numerical magnitude.

q: Physical quantities can be classified as the basic type and the ____ type.
e: Physical quantities can be classified as the basic type and the derived type. The physics in this sentence is built around derived.

q: A derived unit is a unit of measurement formed by combining the basic (or base) units of a ____.
e: A derived unit is a unit of measurement formed by combining the basic (or base) units of a system. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit involving measurement.

q: Standard is something (or) a ____ used as a measure for length, mass and time.
e: Standard is something (or) a reference used as a measure for length, mass and time. The physics in this sentence is built around reference.

q: Unit is a quantity (or) an amount used as a standard of ____.
e: Unit is a quantity (or) an amount used as a standard of measurement. Measurement here means a comparison with an agreed standard that gives you a number. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.
